title: Per-tenant throughput shaping, label evolution and resilient schema migration for inference KPIs
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: As Dedicated and Private customers scale to sustained high QPS, our current metric ingestion path (OTLP -> collector -> aggregator -> TSDB/prom exporter) exhibits two operational gaps: (1) noisy tenant spikes can overwhelm downstream aggregators causing ingestion tail-latency and partial drops; (2) incremental changes to metric labels and KPI schemas for inference (new model tags, routing_policy, cache_hit flags) cause compatibility issues and orphaned time-series, inflating cardinality and storage costs.

Goal: Implement per-tenant throughput shaping and backpressure signals in the ingestion path, plus a controlled schema-evolution workflow that allows safe label additions/removals and deterministic migration of historical series for inference KPIs. The solution must preserve SLOs for latency-sensitive dashboards, limit noisy-tenant blast radius, and enable zero-downtime schema updates for dashboards and alerting rules.

Scope:
- Ingest sidecar/collector changes to surface per-tenant token-aware counters and a tenant backpressure header for upstream clients.
- Aggregator throttling policy that supports token-bucket shaping per tenant and soft-fallback to sample-based summaries when limits are hit.
- Label evolution toolkit: tag-mapping registry with canonical-name aliases, soft-deprecation period, and a migration job to rewrite legacy series into canonical labels in the rollup layer.
- Dashboard and alert reconciliation: scriptable transforms to update Prometheus rules and Grafana panels to use alias mapping.
- End-to-end tests and canary rollout on staging tenants.

Non-goals: full multi-cloud sharding redesign, long-term retention changes, and per-tenant billing integrations (handled separately).
tasks: Design tenant shaping API and header semantics (collab with SDKs)
Implement token-bucket controller in aggregator service with metrics for throttled_count and throttled_duration
Add backpressure header support in the OTLP proxy sidecar and graceful retry guidance in SDK docs
Build label-mapping registry service and admin UI for soft-deprecation windows
Create migration job to rewrite historical series in rollup stage with dry-run mode
Update alert rules and dashboards to support alias mapping and fallback queries
Add e2e tests including high QPS tenant simulation and schema-change scenarios
Run canary with 5 staging tenants, collect metrics and run cutover checklist
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant shaping enforced: aggregator exposes per-tenant throttled_count metric and we can limit sustained ingestion to configured rate without data pipeline failure
Backpressure header is honored by SDKs: dev environment shows clients adjusting request rate when header present
Label mapping registry supports alias queries and shows deprecation windows in UI
Migration job dry-run produces a diff report of series rewrites; full-run rewrites series without data loss and retention metadata preserved
Dashboards show stable latency SLOs (p95 <= 180ms for metric ingest path) during synthetic tenant spikes
Rollout completed to staging tenants with post-mortem and no unresolved alerts
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: High-cardinality explosion if label deprecation is mishandled -> Mitigation: limit allowed new dynamic labels per tenant and gate via feature flag
Risk: Migration job may be heavy on rollup cluster -> Mitigation: run low-priority batch windows, support chunked migration and throttle using cluster resource quotas
Risk: SDK adoption lag for backpressure header -> Mitigation: ship graceful fallback in server: temporarily downsample noisy tenants while SDKs roll out updates
implementation_notes: Aggregator changes will live behind feature flag `tenant_shaping_v2` and default to off.
Use existing token metadata (customer_id + api_key_id) from auth layer to identify tenant; do not add new PII fields.
Store label-mapped aliases in dynamo table `metric_alias_registry` with TTL-based deprecation entries.
Migration job will leverage rollup protobuf transforms already used by `metrics-bridge` component (see design doc).
